newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER WANTS KLINSMANN TO STAY IN MUNICH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER WANTS KLINSMANN TO STAY IN MUNICH.

text.p: Bayern Munich president Franz Beckerbauer said on Saturday he expected goal-starved striker Juergen Klinsmann to stay in Munich for the rest of the current Bundesliga season and beyond.
Beckenbauer, in an interview with the Munich Abendzeitung newspaper, said he hoped Klinsmann would finish his career in Munich.
German media have been filled with reports in recent weeks that Klinsmann was trying to leave Bayern because of tensions with team mates, in particular Lothar Matthaeus.

"Tension and envy happens all the time," Beckenbauer said. "The two just don't get along very well. A striker has to be selfish. Juergen is totally focused on success and is a complete professional. Others could learn from him."

Addressing reports that Klinsmann wanted to leave before the second half of the season starts in February, Beckenbauer said: "I don't even expect him to go after the season ends. I would like him to complete his career here."
The 32-year old former Internazionale and Tottenham Hotspur striker lashed out at his team in a television interview earlier this month, accusing the club of playing too cautiously.

Klinsmann, who has scored just five goals this season, has threatened to leave at the end of the season unless they adopt a more attacking style. Klinsmann said he respected Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni but the Italian's defensive system made it difficult for strikers to operate.

Beckenbauer, in an unusually frank interview, said it had been a mistake to fire coach Otto Rehhagel. Rehhagel was dismissed last April, late in the season, and Beckenbauer temporarily took control. Trapattoni took over this season.
"It was an erroneous decision," Beckenbauer said of the Rehhagel sacking. "And I lost a friend with that."
Beckenbauer, who said he signed a new contract to lead Munich to the year 2000, said he wanted the team to play more attacking football in the future.
"So far there wasn't too much that could be enjoyed," he said of Bayern, who ended the first half of the season top of the league table despite scoring just 27 goals in 17 games.
"I want to see celebrations of soccer -- scores of 6-2 or 5-0," Beckenbauer said.
At the same time, Beckenbauer issued a warning to players who might have been enjoying Munich's nightlife too much during the first half. He said there would be strict curfew controls from now on.

"We're going to start controlling," he said. "The preparations for the next match will begin on Sunday from now on. Anyone caught (out after curfew) will get a verbal warning. Anyone caught a second time will be fined. And if that still doesn't work, someone will be gone."
